subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Silver Bridge Collapse
description: One-minute skill: The Silver Bridge Collapse.

hook.text: On December 15, 1967, the Silver Bridge fell during rush hour. 46 people drowned.

buildup.text: The bridge used eyebar chains instead of wire cables — a less redundant design.

discovery.text: A single eyebar link cracked from corrosion and stress corrosion cracking.

twist.text: One broken link transferred its load to the next. Chain reaction brought it all down.

climax.text: Congress created the National Bridge Inspection Program — every bridge, every two years.

punchline.text: One cracked link killed 46 and changed inspection law forever.

quiz.question: What did the Silver Bridge collapse directly lead to?
options: A nationwide ban on eyebar chain bridges
Creation of the National Bridge Inspection Program
Mandatory replacement of all bridges over 30 years old

details.summary: The Silver Bridge over the Ohio River collapsed without warning on December 15, 1967, killing 46 people during rush hour traffic. Investigation revealed that a single eyebar chain link had failed from stress corrosion cracking.
details.whyItMatters: The Silver Bridge disaster directly led to the National Bridge Inspection Standards requiring biennial inspection of all US bridges. It demonstrated how a single component failure can destroy an entire structure.
takeaways: A single corroded eyebar link failed, collapsing the entire bridge in seconds
Forty-six people died during evening rush hour traffic
The disaster created the US National Bridge Inspection Standards in 1971

faq.question: Why did the failure of one eyebar cause the entire bridge to collapse?
faq.answer: The Silver Bridge used eyebar chain suspension instead of wire cables. Each chain link consisted of only two eyebars, providing no redundancy. When one eyebar cracked, the remaining bar could not carry the doubled load, causing chain failure that propagated through the entire bridge instantly.

faq.question: How did the Silver Bridge collapse change US bridge safety policy?
faq.answer: Congress passed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1968, establishing the National Bridge Inspection Standards requiring all public bridges to be inspected at least every two years. This created the National Bridge Inventory database tracking the condition of over 617,000 bridges.
